 Detailed Forecast
 Synopsis
 Trade winds will strengthen to breezy to strong speeds tonight through Saturday. Weak upper level disturbances should enhance the trade wind showers tonight through Saturday night with showery weather expected across windward and mountain at times. The subtropical ridge will settle in over the island chain by early next week with an extended drying trend and lighter winds in the forecast.
 Discussion
 High pressure building far north of the state will strengthen the trades tonight into Friday with widespread strong trades expected during the day Friday. Wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph will be possible across the windier areas of Maui County and the Big Island. In the upper levels, we have a few short-wave troughs swinging through the state tonight through the weekend, which should enhance the trade wind showers. Thus, windward and mauka areas will likely be showery at times through Saturday, especially tonight through Friday morning and Saturday afternoon through Saturday night. Some of the showers will be carried over leeward areas due to the breezy to strong trade winds.
A strong upper level ridge will build over the state Sunday into early next week and will bring stable and drier conditions. The surface ridge will also get very close to the state, which should decrease the winds and bring variable winds over the state by Tuesday or Wednesday. In the long range, global guidance suggests a front may move into the region around Thanksgiving and increase shower chances. A period of northwest winds may follow thereafter.
 Aviation
 Moderate to breezy trade winds are expected through Friday. An upper level disturbance will also enhance trade wind showers as VFR conditions will prevail with MVFR conditions possible over windward and mauka areas.
AIRMET Sierra has been cancelled for the Big Island. AIRMET Tango may be needed later as trade winds strengthen through the forecast period. No other AIRMETS are currently in effect.
 Marine
 Trade winds will hover in the fresh to locally strong range through this afternoon. Strong high pressure passing north of the islands tonight will lead to more widespread strong trades. As a result, the Small Craft Advisory (SCA) remains in effect for the typically windy waters around Big Island and Maui County through 6 pm, then expands to cover the rest of the coastal zones. Trades then look to decrease later in the weekend and could become light by early next week as the subtropical ridge sinks south over the islands. By the middle of next week, NW winds could ramp up quickly with the potential passing of a cold front. This frontal passage could also have XL swell assoicated with it.
For north facing shores, small north-northwest swell will fade through the day and tiny surf is anticipated on Friday. Another small north-northwest swell is forecast to arrive and build on Saturday, peaking Saturday night into Sunday, with a larger (advisory level) and longer lived northwest swell expected next Tuesday. A potential XL northwest swell is then possible by the middle of next week as models indicate a strong storm force low pressure system developing far north of the islands next week. However, model discrepancies over the strength and position of the fetch are notable at this time, so the size of the swell is still uncertain. And it looks more likely that any large swell will be accompanied by strong NW or N winds.
Rough surf along east-facing shores will hold near seasonal averages today, then increase slightly for Friday and Saturday as trade winds strengthen. A small, long-period swell looks to bring a bump to south shore surf on Friday, and could keep south shore surf slightly elevated through the weekend.
 Fire weather
 Issued at 338 PM HST Thu Nov 19 2026
Trade winds will strengthen tonight into Friday with strong trades expected during the day Friday. Showers riding in with the trades should keep humidity levels near normal for Friday with mainly low to moderate fire weather threat for Friday afternoon. An extended period of drier weather returns for much of next week. Temperature inversion heights should increase to 6,000 to 8,000 feet on Friday due to a weak disturbance passing aloft.

 Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST Friday for Big Island Windward Waters, Kaiwi Channel, Kauai Channel, Kauai Leeward Waters, Kauai Northwest Waters, Kauai Windward Waters, Maui County Leeward Waters, Maui County Windward Waters, Oahu Leeward Waters, Oahu Windward Waters.
Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST Friday for Alenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters, Big Island Southeast Waters, Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel.
